questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: They are made to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
They are made to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
They are made to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

questions.solution:

• Part IV-A (Article 51-A) deals with Fundamental Duties.
 
• This part is added by the 42nd amendment in 1976.

• Now it contains 11 duties after the 86th amendment act, 2002.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and hence can’t be taken to a court of law.

questions.question: How many controls are there globally that influence the climate of a particular zone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Six major controls influence the climate of a particular zone globally:
 
 
• **Latitude:** The latitude of a location determines the angle at which sunlight strikes the Earth's surface. Locations closer to the equator receive more direct sunlight and have warmer temperatures, while locations farther from the equator receive less direct sunlight and have cooler temperatures.
 
• **Altitude**: Altitude refers to the elevation of a location above sea level. As altitude increases, the atmosphere becomes thinner, and air pressure decreases. This reduced air pressure leads to cooler temperatures.
 
• **Distance from the sea:** Land heats up and cools down more quickly than water. Coastal areas tend to have more moderate temperatures than inland areas because the ocean moderates the temperature fluctuations.
 
• **Ocean currents:** Ocean currents transport heat around the globe. Warm ocean currents can bring warmer temperatures to coastal areas, while cold ocean currents can bring cooler temperatures.
 
• **Topography:** Topography refers to the physical features of a landscape, such as mountains and valleys. Mountains can block wind and precipitation patterns, while valleys can trap heat and moisture.
 
• **Prevailing winds:** Prevailing winds are the dominant wind patterns in a region. They can bring warm or cold air masses to an area, influencing the local climate.

• The protonema is responsible for anchorage and absorption of water and nutrients. It also produces buds that develop into gametophytes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nebular hypothesis:-**

 
 
• **The nebular hypothesis proposes that the solar system formed from a giant cloud of gas and dust called a nebula.**
 
• This nebula was mostly composed of hydrogen, with smaller amounts of helium and other elements.
 
• The nebula was also very cold, with temperatures around -270 degrees Celsius (-454 degrees Fahrenheit). 
 
• Over time, the nebula began to collapse under its own gravity. As the nebula collapsed, it spun faster and faster.
 
• This spinning caused the nebula to flatten out into a disk, with the sun forming at the center of the disk.

• **Gas hypothesis:-**

 
 
• It was proposed by Immanuel Kant in the 18th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a cloud of gas that had been heated by a passing star.**
 
• The heat from the star caused the gas to expand, and this expansion eventually caused the cloud to collapse.
 
• As the cloud collapsed, it spun faster and faster, and this spinning caused the cloud to flatten out into a disk.
 
• The sun formed at the center of the disk, and the planets formed from the remaining material in the disk.
 
 
 
• **Solar hypothesis:-**
 
 
• It was proposed by René Descartes in the 17th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a vortex of matter that was ejected from the sun. **
 
• The vortex of matter eventually cooled and solidified, and this solidified matter formed the planets and other bodies in the solar system.
 
 
 
• **Cloud hypothesis:-**
 
 
• It was proposed by Thomas Wright in the 18th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a cloud of dust that had been ejected from a much larger star. **
 
• The cloud of dust eventually cooled and solidified, and this solidified matter formed the planets and other bodies in the solar system.
